## Eval launch commands (Marin)

These commands require an Iris account with access to the `marin` controller and the `cw-rno2a`
federated cluster. `MODEL_CONFIG` must be an absolute path to a Marin model-catalog YAML file whose
model and tokenizer revisions are immutable. The model must support a 73,728-token context for MRCR.
The checkout below is the public campaign revision based on the pinned Marin `main` commit above. It
adds the Evalchemy revision that correctly applies the zero-shot MMLU-Pro policy.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/marin-community/marin.git
cd marin
git checkout ba2fef7443dd5fad1b1a35402982e1c4ce71c8c0
uv sync --all-packages

export MODEL_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/pinned-model.yaml
export TOGETHER_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_API_KEY="$TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_BASE_URL=https://api.together.xyz/v1
export JUDGE_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-120b

POLICY_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)

write_chat_config() {
  config_name=$1
  task_name=$2
  runtime_extra=$3
  max_tokens=$4
  max_length=$5
  {
    echo "tasks: [$task_name]"
    echo "task_options:"
    echo "  $task_name:"
    echo "    num_fewshot: 0"
    echo "    task_alias: $config_name"
    echo "    generation: true"
    echo "apply_chat_template: true"
    echo "batch_size: 1"
    echo "seed: 42"
    echo "max_tokens: $max_tokens"
    if [ "$max_length" != "default" ]; then
      echo "max_length: $max_length"
    fi
    echo "runtime_extras: [$runtime_extra]"
  } > "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/$config_name.yaml"
}

write_chat_config mmlu-pro MMLUPro mmlupro 32768 65536
write_chat_config gpqa-diamond GPQADiamond gpqadiamond 32768 default
write_chat_config cruxeval CruxEval cruxeval 2048 default
write_chat_config financebench FinanceBench financebench 4096 default
write_chat_config ifbench IFBench ifbench 1024 default
write_chat_config mrcr MRCR mrcr 4096 73728

# Deterministic single-run Evalchemy and lm-eval-harness evaluations.
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --evals math500,humanevalplus,mbppplus,olympiadbench,gsm8k-0shot,mmlu,piqa,winogrande,openbookqa,boolq,truthfulqa,triviaqa \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated

# AIME24: ten independent launches; Evalchemy generates ten responses per question in each launch.
for seed in $(seq 42 51); do
  uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
    --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
    --evals aime24 \
    --seed "$seed" \
    --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
    --priority interactive \
    --version eval-policy-updated
done

# Policy additions that are not registered as named Marin eval keys at the pinned Marin commit.
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/mmlu-pro.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/gpqa-diamond.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/cruxeval.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/financebench.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/ifbench.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/mrcr.yaml" \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated

# The campaign's five Harbor policies are pinned on its public experiment branch.
for config_name in swebench-recovery ot-tblite-recovery tb2-recovery simpleqa-recovery ds-1000-local; do
  curl -fsSL \
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/8aa9a354d30abbda89a7756e11c1a37037aa8a65/experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/$config_name.yaml" \
    -o "experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/$config_name.yaml"
done

# Select the policy's deterministic seed-42 mini datasets from the pinned Harbor registry.
export HARBOR_REGISTRY_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/harbor/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a/registry.json
uv run python - "$HARBOR_REGISTRY_URL" <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

registry_url = sys.argv[1]
config_dir = Path("experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor")
for filename, dataset_name in (
    ("simpleqa-recovery.yaml", "simpleqa"),
    ("ds-1000-local.yaml", "ds-1000"),
):
    path = config_dir / filename
    policy = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
    policy["datasets"] = [
        {
            "name": dataset_name,
            "version": "mini-200",
            "registry_url": registry_url,
        }
    ]
    if dataset_name == "ds-1000":
        # DS-1000's registry tasks must build their pinned Dockerfiles; no
        # published prebuilt image is available for this dataset version.
        policy.setdefault("environment", {})["force_build"] = True
    path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(policy, sort_keys=False))
PY

uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/swebench-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/ot-tblite-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/tb2-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/simpleqa-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/ds-1000-local.yaml \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated
```

## Eval launch commands (Standalone)

The standalone path requires an OpenAI-compatible endpoint reachable from both the local evaluator
and Daytona sandboxes. `MODEL_BASE_URL` is the API root ending in `/v1`; `MODEL_ID` must match the
model name returned by its `/models` endpoint; and `TOKENIZER_ID` must be an immutable Hugging Face
model or tokenizer revision. Evalchemy executes generated code for HumanEvalPlus and MBPPPlus.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy.git
cd evalchemy
git checkout 65c80022b8be98012a4ce6cd98a5168a7a58d99e
uv sync --python 3.12 --extra benchmarks --extra serve-eval

export MODEL_BASE_URL=https://example-model-endpoint.invalid/v1
export MODEL_ID="REPLACE_WITH_SERVED_MODEL_NAME"
export MODEL_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_MODEL_ENDPOINT_API_KEY"
export TOKENIZER_ID="REPLACE_WITH_HUGGING_FACE_TOKENIZER_ID"
export TOKENIZER_REVISION="REPLACE_WITH_IMMUTABLE_TOKENIZER_REVISION"
export TOGETHER_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_API_KEY="$TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_BASE_URL=https://api.together.xyz/v1
export JUDGE_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-120b

mkdir -p results/evalchemy

run_chat_eval() {
  task_name=$1
  num_fewshot=$2
  max_tokens=$3
  max_length=$4
  seed=$5
  output_name=$6
  shift 6
  uv run eval \
    --model local-chat-completions \
    --model_args "model=$MODEL_ID,base_url=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}/chat/completions,api_key=$MODEL_API_KEY,tokenizer=$TOKENIZER_ID,revision=$TOKENIZER_REVISION,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=8,timeout=1800,max_length=$max_length" \
    --tasks "$task_name" \
    --num_fewshot "$num_fewshot" \
    --batch_size 1 \
    --seed "$seed" \
    --max_length "$max_length" \
    --max_tokens "$max_tokens" \
    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=$max_tokens" \
    --apply_chat_template \
    --log_samples \
    --output_path "results/evalchemy/$output_name" \
    "$@"
}

run_completion_eval() {
  task_name=$1
  num_fewshot=$2
  max_tokens=$3
  max_length=$4
  uv run eval \
    --model local-completions \
    --model_args "model=$MODEL_ID,base_url=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}/completions,api_key=$MODEL_API_KEY,tokenizer=$TOKENIZER_ID,revision=$TOKENIZER_REVISION,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=8,timeout=1800,max_length=$max_length" \
    --tasks "$task_name" \
    --num_fewshot "$num_fewshot" \
    --batch_size 1 \
    --seed 42 \
    --max_length "$max_length" \
    --max_tokens "$max_tokens" \
    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=$max_tokens" \
    --log_samples \
    --output_path "results/evalchemy/$task_name"
}

run_chat_eval MATH500 0 8192 73664 42 math500
for seed in $(seq 42 51); do
  run_chat_eval AIME24 0 8192 73664 "$seed" "aime24-seed-$seed"
done
run_chat_eval HumanEvalPlus 0 1024 73664 42 humanevalplus --confirm_run_unsafe_code
```

## Standards for presenting Marin evals

* For each benchmark, plot Snowball perf, along with baseline(s) perf, on an x-y scatterplot, with y being perf and x being total training FLOPS
* Use 6ND proxy for pretraining and SFT FLOPS, and 6 * max_tokens_per_rollout / max_context_length * n_rollouts * active_params proxy for RL FLOPS
* In a separate standalone table, include all raw scores in XX.y format, with 95% confidence intervals derived from the trial count -- do not leave gaps, use table captions for results that require further context, use the exact same model family in the table as was present in the x-y scatterplot(s)
* Eval results are reportable IFF the eval in question completed with <10% of trials encountering infrastructure errors
* Eval results are reportable IFF they include provenance, in the form of model traces, and where available, verifier traces
* Any eval result that is publicly presented should clearly distinguish whether the benchmarks are in-distribution (part of the dev set), held out, or a mix of the two
* Any eval result that is publicly presented in a major release should report on *all* ID and OOD benchmarks, avoiding cherry picking, substitution, or new evals outside of a formal policy update
* For active development and internal communication, it is fine to define working subsets of the ID benchmarks and report on those in isolation

## Future considerations

* We would like to post-train multiple Snowball checkpoints, experimenting with different degrees of compute applied to post-training, to establish trade-off lines / domains
* We would like to think about a "marin model card" that would set minimum standards for true open development

👍 

I'm on board with the set of evaluations and how to run them, and I like that we'll have a policy for what we can look at. My proposal re pins:

* We define this as Marin Eval Policy v0.1
* Pins indicate the behavior now
* If we need to move the pins (to update to a new version of Iris, etc)
  - We rerun the eval suites with a representative model(s) - Qwen + Snowball
  - If the suites are identical (within noise), we update pins in place
  - If not, we need to bump the version
* Results should be reported at a particular version
* Updating the version should be infrequent but acceptable: a totally broken eval for example

I think the bulk of the value here is being transparent about all of the appropriate parameters and command lines for running we're using for the evaluations, and that we'll do our best to keep these aligned. I want us to balance the desire for replication with flexibility for making code changes, so hopefully the above tradeoff seems fair.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
`build_model_args` in `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py:72` sends `tokenizer=<checkpoint>,tokenizer_backend=huggingface` on every lm-eval route and never passes `trust_remote_code`. On the chat route the endpoint applies the chat template, so the client tokenizer is unused, but lm-eval still loads it at model init. Two cohort models fail every Evalchemy eval at that step, on Evalchemy 07c7cce as well as the older pin:

- google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it: `Failed to initialize model: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'` (Gemma 4 tokenizer metadata against the client's Transformers 4).
- moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct: `Failed to initialize model: The repository ... contains custom code which must be executed to correctly load the model`.

marin-community/evalchemy#140 fixed both in Evalchemy's own serve-eval runner (`tokenizer_backend=none` for chat, `trust_remote_code=True` for completions), but Marin's eval child calls the `evalchemy` CLI with its own argument string, so the fix never reaches Marin launches. Eval configs cannot work around it: `tokenizer_backend` is in `RESERVED_ENDPOINT_MODEL_ARGS`, so `extra_model_args` may not override it.

Reproduce:
1. `uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model-config <catalog yaml for google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it> --evals math500 --federated_cluster cw-rno2a --priority interactive --version test`
2. The `eval-math500-*` child exits 1 with `Failed to initialize model: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'`.

Expected: chat-route launches send `tokenizer_backend=none` and no `tokenizer`; completion-route launches keep the local tokenizer for loglikelihood scoring and pass `trust_remote_code=True`. Both models then evaluate.

Fix applied on the eval-policy release branch as marin-community/marin@97dd188d5e (`benfeuer/bump-evalchemy-sandbox-fix`), with a test in `tests/evals/test_evalchemy_config.py`; it needs to land on `main`.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Allow Grug MoE backends to exclude padded positions from expert dispatch, capacity accounting, and expert computation. Carry token validity from the model's attention mask into the MoE path; a padding token ID alone is not sufficient because the same ID can appear at a valid position.

In the Snowball 67B RL trial on 32 H100s (PP4/EP8, ragged all-to-all, capacity factor 2), the first microbatch contained 42,435 padded positions out of 68,160 (62.26%). Routing rejected 1,559,713 of 7,088,640 assignments across 26 layers, and the no-drop guard stopped the run before an optimizer update. Padding contributes to capacity demand; the fraction of rejected assignments belonging to valid tokens has not been measured. The ragged backend reports these as sender drops, although clipping is applied to receiver expert-chunk capacity.

Packing is being added separately. For the complete 512-trajectory capture, Levanter's packing reduces overall padding from 55.10% to 15.49% after alignment to eight GPUs, so residual padding still needs handling.

Done when:

- Invalid positions consume no expert capacity and produce no dispatched expert rows or expert-parameter gradient contributions.
- When valid assignments fit capacity, valid-token outputs, loss, and gradients match an equivalent unpadded, dropless computation within existing numerical tolerances. Adding padding does not change which valid assignments are accepted, including when valid demand exceeds capacity.
- Tests cover mixed sequence lengths, packed segment boundaries, all-padding local shards, and distributed forward/backward execution without collective mismatches.
- Routing metrics distinguish valid assignments, skipped padding, and genuine capacity drops. A padded workload benchmark reports the memory and runtime effect.

Start with `moe_mlp` in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py` and the ragged backend in `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`.

Evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/users/dlwh/skyrl/migration/june-ragged-67b-benchmark-20260907-02/drops.json`, `capture-padding.json` under the same prefix, and `s3://marin-us-east-02a/users/dlwh/skyrl/migration/june-packing-census-20260907-01/census.json`.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read fix-issue and commit skills, AGENTS.md
- [x] Investigate Grug MoE dispatch/capacity path and how token validity flows
- [x] Assess scope — feature-scale (multi-backend + metrics + distributed tests + benchmark), no PR
- [x] Post root-cause analysis and proposed approach

## Research

The MoE path has no concept of token validity. `moe_mlp` and every EP backend accept only `x [T,D]`, `selected_experts [T,K]`, and `combine_weights [T,K]`; padded positions are ordinary rows and route like any token ([`grug_moe.py` L146-161](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py#L146-L161)). In the ragged backend, demand is `group_sizes = bincount(flat_selected, length=num_experts)` and capacity is `ceil(capacity_factor * tokens_per_shard * topk)`, so padded assignments count as real demand, get clipped against capacity, are dispatched and run through the expert MLP, and contribute expert-parameter gradients ([`ep_ragged_all_to_all.py` L328-345](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L328-L345)). The reported drops are then `sum(group_sizes) - accepted_local`, which conflates padding with genuine capacity drops of valid tokens ([L420-422](lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py#L420-L422)) — consistent with the 62% padding and 22% rejected-assignments observation and the no-drop guard tripping. As the issue notes, a padding token id cannot identify padding (the same id can appear at a valid position), so validity must come from the attention mask / segment ids.

## Proposed approach (for review before implementation)

Thread an optional validity mask and make invalid positions consume no capacity, no dispatched rows, and no expert-parameter gradients, while keeping all buffer shapes statically sized on the worst case so no collective shapes change.

1. **API.** Add `token_valid: Bool[Array, "T"] | None = None` to `MoEExpertMlp.__call__` → `moe_mlp` → each `_moe_mlp_ep_*_local` and `_moe_mlp_local`. `None` means all-valid, preserving current behavior and existing tests. Derive the mask in the model from the attention mask / segment ids (grug attention already exposes `segment_ids` metadata via `thd_segment_metadata_from_segment_ids`).
2. **Ragged backend.** Before `bincount`, remap invalid tokens' `flat_selected` to a sentinel expert (`num_experts`) so `bincount(length=num_experts)` drops them from `group_sizes`. Their sorted assignments land past every real group, so `_expert_granular_a2a_params` never sends them — no receiver capacity, no dispatched rows, no expert-param grads. `[TK]`/`[C]` buffers stay static; only the counts feeding `group_sizes`/clipping change. Zero invalid tokens' `combine_weights` as belt-and-suspenders (the unpermute already reads unwritten slots as zero).
3. **Other backends.** Apply the equivalent capacity-accounting exclusion to `ep_fixed_all_to_all`, `ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, `ep_ring`, `ep_deepep`, and `local` — each computes capacity/clipping differently.
4. **Metrics.** Extend `CapacityOverflow` (or the routing metrics) to distinguish valid assignments dispatched, skipped-padding assignments, and genuine capacity drops of valid tokens, replacing the padding-conflated `dropped_local`.
5. **Invariants to preserve** (from Done-when): with `token_valid=None` outputs are bit-identical to today; when valid demand fits capacity, valid outputs/loss/grads match an unpadded dropless reference within existing tolerances; adding padding never changes which valid assignments are accepted (the sentinel keeps valid group prefixes and clip decisions independent of padding).
6. **Tests / benchmark.** Mixed sequence lengths, packed segment boundaries, an all-padding local shard (zero output, no collective mismatch), and distributed forward/backward equivalence vs. an unpadded reference; plus a padded-workload benchmark reporting memory and runtime.

Files: `grug_moe.py`, `_moe/{ep_ragged_all_to_all,ep_fixed_all_to_all,ep_fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all,ep_ring,ep_deepep,local,common}.py`, and the training MoE MLP block that threads the mask. issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Canonical evaluation model configs expose tensor and data parallelism, but not pipeline parallelism. This prevents the blessed `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` path from serving an evaluation model across multiple Iris tasks.

The immediate failure is [GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 on TB2.1](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/20260813-011602-glm-5.2-awq-int4-glm-5.2-awq-int4-tb21-aa-7bc9). At `max_model_len: 1048576`, TP8 on one H100x8 node loaded 62.35 GiB of weights per rank, then vLLM failed before any trial ran:

```
ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization`
```

PP2 with TP8 inside each node would reduce stage-local weight memory while retaining NVLink for tensor parallelism. Marin already has Iris gang rendezvous and native vLLM PP support from #7758. That implementation is currently exercised as PP2/TP1/DP8 for Grug; its helper fixes local TP to 1, and the evaluation path does not call it.

The remaining gaps are visible in [`ServeConfig`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/model_config.py#L63-L89), [GPU topology validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/hardware.py#L170-L180), and [evaluation serving lowering](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/serving_config.py#L258-L278). They model one GPU slice and validate only `TP × DP`.

Done when:

- Evaluation model YAML can declare pipeline parallelism separately from per-node tensor and data parallelism.
- The launcher validates per-node GPU use and total gang geometry.
- PP2/TP8 lowers to two coscheduled H100x8 Iris tasks and starts one distributed vLLM endpoint.
- Dry-run output and durable evaluation records preserve the resolved PP, TP, DP, task count, and per-task accelerator shape.
- A behavioral test covers a multi-node evaluation topology and rejects inconsistent geometry before submission.

Tracked from #8083.

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Architecture and plan for the evaldash issues, peer-reviewed as requested: https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6bfst8b/artifacts/evaldash-stats-engine (rev 2)

The four subissues are the same gap seen from four angles. Evaldash has no representation of *a measurement and how much of it happened* — a matrix cell is `value: float | None`, so there is nowhere to put "236 of 240 intended trials, 4 agent timeouts", and nothing to filter or aggregate on except presence. #8084 needs that representation to admit a partial run, #8085 needs it to qualify an aggregate, #8086 needs it to decide which result is admissible, #8087 needs a query object over it.

So the pre-work is one engine, shared by the eval runners and the dashboard: a typed measurement carrying its item counts and interval, plus an explicit selection query over a set of measurements. Each issue is then a call into it.

**Statistical core.** One estimand: the success rate over the items a run set out to grade. With `c = n_scored / n_attempted`, θ splits into an identified part and an unidentified one, and the missing part gets bounded rather than imputed — missingness correlates with task difficulty, which is exactly why #8084 needs a gate rather than an average. The reported interval is Wilson on the scored items, scaled by `c` and widened by `1 − c`, with an Imbens–Manski critical value so it covers the parameter at 95% instead of over-covering at ~97.5%. Width is at least `1 − c`: a run that graded 92.3% of its trials reports an interval at least 7.7 points wide however many trials it ran.

**Three things fall out that are worth flagging before implementation.**

1. Harbor already publishes a biased number, and the gate would expose it. `_aggregate` divides by `len(trials)` while an errored trial is read back with reward 0.0, so `accuracy` scores every timeout as a wrong answer — the Manski lower bound, computed by accident and labelled a point estimate. It is masked today only because any failed trial aborts the run. Relaxing that without fixing the denominator would ship the bias. The intended-trial count also cannot come from the result glob: a trial that dies before writing leaves no file, so the runs with the worst attrition would report perfect coverage.
2. Ranking cannot use `k / n_scored`. It is a complete-case estimate, so ranking on it rewards a model for timing out on hard items — #8085's complaint re-entering through the sort key. Ranking uses the interval's lower bound. At `c = 1` the two coincide, so the 368 evalchemy runs are unaffected.
3. A 90% gate admits results for display but cannot support ordering claims. Resolving a 5-point gap between two models needs coverage above 0.975 on both, and 2 points needs 0.99. Display admission and comparison admission are two thresholds, not one.

**Evidence.** Everything above is checked against the 387 records under `gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals` (CoreWeave needs credentials this session did not have). Item counts are already there — 1204 of 1249 per-task metric dicts carry `sample_len`, and Harbor carries `total`/`solved` — so the primary adapter is the record, not the archive, which matters because only 6 of 387 runs have a finestore archive today. A cross-check worth knowing about: the llama-3.1-8b mmlu record has 124 task entries because the run wrote the whole 62-entry panel twice, once under `mmlu_5shot` and once under a task directory named `tmp6jnnx8cc`, scoring 0.63502 and 0.63488. Benchmark identity cannot be the raw evalchemy task directory, and that duplicate looks like a separate launcher bug.

**Peer review** changed the design materially, so the artifact records it. Adopted: the Imbens–Manski correction; asymmetric difference bounds; demoting paired comparison, which provably buys zero attrition-width reduction; the Harbor denominator fixes; dropping a fleet-max denominator inference and a new Postgres table that would have been write-only; and moving the engine out of `lib/finestore` — `marin-core` already depends on `marin-finestore`, so an engine there naming `RunStatus` would create a distribution cycle and break that wheel's CI leg. It lives in `marin/evaluation/` under the same import-light contract as `records.py` and is vendored into the dashboard image by one `COPY`; "on top of finestore" holds on the data path, not the package path. One of my own claims did not survive: the apparent mmlu panel drift between models was my triple-count of group and leaf rows.

Proceeding to implementation as one PR: engine and tests, the record coverage contract, the Harbor gate, the evaldash panel API, then the SPA. Item-level tallies, paired comparison intervals, and evidence-based suspect-zero detection are deferred and will be filed separately.

comments.author: weaverbot
comments.body:
🤖 Plan and first PR are up.

**Artifact (architecture + plan, peer-reviewed twice):** https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6bfst8b/artifacts/evaldash-stats-engine
**PR:** #8122 — CI green.

## What the four issues have in common

evaldash had no representation of *a measurement and how much of it happened* — a cell was `value: float | None`. That single gap produces all four symptoms: a Harbor batch with one timed-out trial in 240 is either discarded or silently scored as if the trial were wrong (#8084); a cross-benchmark mean is reported without saying which benchmarks, at which metric, or what it did about the ones a model never ran (#8085); a partial re-run hides older results that are still the newest available for their own benchmark (#8086); and filtering has nowhere to express "complete coverage only" because coverage isn't a thing the data carries (#8087).

So the PR is mostly the engine, with the four issues as applications of it — the pre-work-plus-applications shape you suggested, in one PR rather than five.

## The engine

Each result is stored as sufficient statistics (items graded, items attempted, correct count, recorded dispersion, per-cause counts of ungraded items) and intervals are derived on read. The estimand is θ over the items a run *set out* to grade. With `c = n_scored / n_attempted`, `θ = c·θ_obs + (1−c)·θ_miss`, and θ_miss is bounded to [0, 1] rather than imputed — a trial that times out is more likely to be a hard trial, so imputing anything for it is a guess about difficulty. The interval therefore widens by at least `1−c`: admitting a partial batch costs width proportional to what was missed, which is your "unknown interval around the missed answers" made concrete.

Two details worth flagging:

- The critical value is Imbens–Manski, not the ordinary 1.96. Applying the two-sided quantile to an interval that already spans an unidentified region covers the identified *set* at 95% and over-covers the parameter (~97.5% at realistic coverage rates). Because Δ is known exactly here rather than estimated, the usual objection to that correction doesn't apply.
- Binary metrics use Wilson, because eval results really do sit at the boundary — 0 of 8 agentic trials has a normal interval of *zero width* and a Wilson interval of [0.000, 0.324].

Every ordering in the system sorts on the interval's lower bound, so losing items cannot buy rank.

## Per issue

**#8084** — Harbor takes its attempted-trial count from the job's own bookkeeping (counting result files misses every trial that died before writing one, so preempted runs would report perfect coverage), divides rates by the trials a verifier actually graded, and keeps the per-error-type counts of the rest. A batch below a 90% completion gate fails as `infra_failed` and still records its coverage, so the rejection reads as counts. Run detail shows the breakdown. An unreadable job record leaves the count *unknown* rather than equal to results-found — the runs where it's unknown are exactly the interrupted ones a found-count would certify as complete.

**#8085** — No cross-benchmark mean is shown at all unless a caller names a missing-data policy, and one that is shown renders its panel, per-benchmark metrics, and policy inline. The primary surface is a panel table: one row per model, one column per benchmark. `ComparePage`'s client-side mean, which scored a missing shared benchmark as 0, is gone; comparison goes through the engine and answers orderings with a difference interval per benchmark rather than two error bars to eyeball.

**#8086** — Each benchmark comes from the newest run that clears the request's admission rules, across cohorts, so a partial re-run no longer hides results still newest for their own benchmark. `cohort=` pins to one launch when you want that instead. Every cell carries its run id, version, git sha, and timestamp; a `(model, benchmark)` with no admitted cell reports why and links the offending run, so an empty cell is explained rather than blank.

**#8087** — Benchmark column selection, a one-action complete-panel filter, cohort selection, model search, and run-metadata facets (accelerator/platform/backend/mechanism/user) are all in the request, so a panel is a shareable URL. The active ones render as removable chips: a number on screen should never be the product of a filter the reader can't see.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Filed as follow-ups: item-level tallies so binary intervals stop depending on inverting a rate (#8123), paired comparisons on shared items (#8124), the evalchemy launcher writing the same mmlu panel under two task directories (#8125), attempted-item counts for lm-eval runs so their intervals stop being sampling-only (#8126), and pyrefly/test-selection coverage for the evaldash server tree (#8127).

One caveat on #8126 worth knowing before reading the dashboard: today nearly every evalchemy run's interval is labelled `sampling_only`, because lm-eval records how many documents it graded but never how many it attempted. That's the honest label — completeness is unknown, not established — but it applies fleet-wide until the producers record the count.

The eval registry declares the family, `gsm8k` and `gsm8k-0shot` both naming `gsm8k`, and the launcher writes it into each run's `eval.family`, so the dashboard groups columns from what the records say instead of a table it maintains. The panel a request answers is that one variant per family, so coverage, `complete=1`, the aggregate and Compare all describe the columns on screen; cells stay keyed by exact eval name and keep their own metric, cohort and harness version. Records written before the field parse unchanged.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body: TL;DR: filed #9192 — a retried single-task evalchemy run shows the mean of its canonical and scratch attempts as the run's overall score. Run 20260806-193519-qwen3-8b-olympiadbench-5172 displays 10.0 where its two attempts scored 6.67% and 13.33%, with the item count doubled to 60 for a 30-item task. The read-side same-task dedup keys on the leaf task name, which never matches a bare `tmp<random>` scratch leaf on single-task runs, and the record was written with the scratch entry present. The same run renders every sample "ungraded"; that producer-side gap is tracked in marin-community/evalchemy#128.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 TL;DR from the 2026-09-17 eval-policy baseline cohort (RELEASE.md in the eval-policy-09-17 experiment):

- marin-community/evalchemy#136, fixed by marin-community/evalchemy#137 (merged as d0e99df): HumanEvalPlus and MBPPPlus graded every sample as failed since evalchemy#111, so `pass@1` read 0.0 for every model. The spawned grading worker had no numpy loaded and `reliability_guard` nulls `os.putenv`, which numpy's first import calls. Every HumanEvalPlus/MBPPPlus score from Marin pins between evalchemy 8fdf43f and d0e99df is invalid; the cohort is rerunning them.
- marin-community/evalchemy#141: one malformed model response (`endpoint reported 1 malformed_model_response failure(s)`) fails the whole task and discards the other samples. Evalchemy should log and record per-sample failures rather than kill the task.
- #9227: Marin's Evalchemy client loads the checkpoint tokenizer on chat routes, which fails model init for google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct. evalchemy#140 fixed Evalchemy's own runner but not this client. Fixed on the release branch as 97dd188d5e; needs landing on `main`.
- #9070 / #9197: the pinned launcher forwards no judge credentials, so FinanceBench preflight fails with `JUDGE_API_KEY is required`. The release branch forwards `JUDGE_API_KEY`, `JUDGE_BASE_URL`, and `JUDGE_MODEL` through `EVAL_ENV_KEYS` as a stopgap until #9197 lands.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body: 🤖 One more from the same cohort: #9229. The Harbor preflight rejects `datasets[].name: hf://...` since #9145, because it no longer masks Hugging Face datasets before calling `Job.create`, so `swebench-recovery.yaml` fails validation with "Package name must be in 'org/name' format" and the launcher refuses the launch. Harbor's validator is unchanged between pins; the regression is in Marin's `trial_driver.py`. SWE-bench recovery is blocked for the eight cohort models that had not completed it before the release moved onto `main`.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Three more from the 2026-09-17 cohort relaunch loop:

- marin-community/evalchemy#142: IFBench fails every run with `scored task produced no sample records`; its grader never records per-sample results under the #131 contract, so the task is discarded after grading.
- marin-community/evalchemy#143: with `tokenizer_backend=none` (the #140 mode, mirrored in Marin's client at 97dd188d5e), the #132 prompt-length preflight calls `apply_chat_template` on a missing tokenizer and fails lm-eval-native chat tasks such as triviaqa. Evalchemy's own chat benchmarks are unaffected.
- marin-community/harbor#157: terminus-2 does `dict.update` on `extra_body`, but Marin's catalog stores it as a JSON string (`AgentConfig.agent_kwargs` is `Mapping[str, str]`) and `harbor_model_agent_kwargs` forwards it verbatim, so every Harbor trial fails at agent construction for every thinking-mode model. Same code at both Harbor pins. Either Harbor decodes the string or Marin does before the overlay.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Establish a reproducible baseline for an existing Snowball terminal agent on established computational biology benchmarks, with frozen weights. Start with a small diagnostic pilot, then expand to a fixed evaluation set for comparing subsequent checkpoints. Separate scientific errors from agent, serving, environment, and grading failures. Together AI is available for LLM judging, so judge access no longer limits benchmark selection. Prioritize BixBench's existing Harbor CLI adapter as the primary-suite candidate, continue the Terminal-Bench-Science smoke test, and validate ScienceAgentBench's bioinformatics tasks next.

## Description

Computational biology tasks combine coding, statistical analysis, scientific judgment, and domain tools. Snowball already has a post-trained terminal-agent checkpoint and measured performance with its matching harness in [#8225](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8225). We need to establish how that capability transfers to biological analysis.

The proposed starting model is [Snowball 67B-A2B Nemotron-Terminal, step 1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888/tree/680bec3ade494b61ead6861fa24fc4071f8dc294), evaluated through Harbor with its matching Terminus-2 terminal-agent harness. Confirm whether a newer checkpoint is preferred before fixing the baseline. Record each checkpoint separately.

Use Marin's existing evaluation launcher and Harbor integration where available. This issue tracks benchmark selection, integration readiness, runs, and findings. Substantial adapter changes can be linked as separate implementation work. New benchmarks, training, and tool-free biology evaluations are outside the first milestone.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure how often Snowball completes computational biology tasks under a fixed execution budget, and identify the dominant causes of failure. The initial baseline measures existing capability; it does not establish the causal benefit of coding training or imply an absence of biology exposure in the checkpoint's training data.

Scorer code and release inventories were checked on September 14–15, 2026. These readiness assessments are source inspections except for the GeneBench-Pro scorer checks and Terminal-Bench-Science oracle run described below. No Snowball biology baseline has completed.

September 17 planning update: Together AI is the available route for LLM judging; provider integration has not yet been tested in this effort. Its [OpenAI-compatible API](https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/openai-compatibility) supports chat and structured outputs with a Together endpoint, API key, and model ID. A judge requirement is no longer a reason to defer a benchmark. Configure and test each evaluator's provider integration, including vision where needed. Pin the judge model, prompt, and settings; check reference, deliberately wrong, and ambiguous answers before a pilot. A replacement judge defines a separately reported evaluation variant until score comparability has been established.

Priority reflects integration readiness and scientific coverage. `Next check` identifies immediate readiness work; `Follow-up` covers additional integration or complementary coverage; `Resolve assets/protocol` requires obtaining restricted scoring assets or defining a grading procedure. Input access and resource requirements still need validation for each selected task.

| Priority | Benchmark and capability | Released scorer and reference material | Access and judge requirements | Harbor readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Next check: primary candidate | [BixBench v1.5, Harbor CLI](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/adapters/bixbench): notebook-derived biological analysis questions | [Harbor judge code](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/0d67ca4b59206aca2734bf9fe0260ca79e08acb4/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) and public reference answers are available. The adapter grades open answers with an LLM, including numeric/range answers. Upstream also releases a [deterministic multiple-choice grader](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/49311180bdacb324c596f2e07596c126f2004008/bixbench/graders.py). | The pinned grader uses the OpenAI SDK, an API-key variable, a configurable model name, and structured-response parsing. Connect it to Together AI and validate parsing and grading. Upstream multiple-choice scoring uses a different question/answer protocol. | Adapter exists upstream and in Marin's fork. First primary-suite candidate: validate the Together judge and one task, then select a prespecified pilot across data capsules. Report the judge variant explicitly; the CLI protocol differs from the original notebook leaderboard. |
| Next check: smoke test | [Terminal-Bench-Science, life sciences](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science): scientific workflows | Task-specific executable tests and reference fixtures are released. For the inspected [genomic-model-ranking task](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science/tree/ff55a1b0810a5cc2ebac3ebb007cbe6a26aa2e3b/tasks/life-sciences/biology/genomic-model-ranking/tests), pytest checks predictions, rankings, and executable submissions against supplied fixtures and thresholds. | That task's verifier runs without network access or a judge API. Check other tasks individually. | Harbor-native. This task's oracle passed through Marin's Harbor/Daytona setup; the Snowball attempt awaits serving. Validate each additional task individually. |
| Next check | [ScienceAgentBench, bioinformatics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080): Python analysis and scientific computing | The pinned [adapter manifest](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters/scienceagentbench/task_manifest.json) lists 27 bioinformatics tasks: 11 Category A deterministic and 16 Category B visual. The adapter supports reference programs and task-specific numerical/file checks. | Category A needs no LLM judge; Category B defaults to GPT-4o vision. A Together replacement for Category B needs image-input and grading validation. Benchmark inputs and gold assets require a separate SharePoint download. Some tasks need GPU or additional RAM; the adapter reports CPU oracle failures. | [Adapter exists](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters/scienceagentbench/README.md) upstream and in Marin's fork. Stage and oracle-test a CPU-suitable bioinformatics task. Include visual tasks once the vision judge is validated; selection need not be restricted to deterministic tasks. |
| Follow-up | [scBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09063): single-cell analysis from workflow snapshots | [Current release](https://github.com/latchbio/scbench/tree/0bc34032bfa402dad29fc40b4cf10ea8fc03193e) contains six example tasks with grader configurations and targets; [shared grader code](https://github.com/latchbio/latch-eval-tools) is public. All six examples use numerical tolerances; the shared library also supports label and distribution checks. | Correctness grading needs no LLM. Inputs are referenced through Latch data nodes; download/access has not been validated. Full suite is withheld. Current README describes 195 tasks/six public examples; the paper describes 394/thirty. Pin and report the actual release. | No adapter found. Follow-up port after checking data access; report a public-subset score separately from the paper's full-suite result. |
| Follow-up | [GeneBench-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package): judgment-heavy genomics and quantitative biology | Ten public cases include [reference_grader.py](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package/blob/eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2/reference_grader.py), reference answers, schemas, and tolerances. Uses numeric, integer, and exact-match checks. Boolean `passed` is authoritative; `score` is diagnostic. | Ungated public package; grader uses the Python standard library and no API key. The full 129-task suite is not contained in this release. | No adapter found. Concrete candidate for a small port: scorer checks passed below. Public cases support development and reproduction, with results reported separately from the full benchmark. |
| Follow-up | [SpatialBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21907): spatial transcriptomics analysis | Pinned [public sample](https://github.com/latchbio/spatialbench/tree/5042c4f3ee597da1590650c7b894d068ae968e26/example_evals) contains 16 task JSONs plus a manifest. Inspected tasks include deterministic grader configurations and targets, using the shared Latch grader library. | No LLM needed for the inspected graders. Inputs use Latch data pointers; downloads remain untested. Current README describes a 159-task full suite that is withheld. | No adapter found. Candidate public-subset port after data access and selected graders are validated. |
| Follow-up | [BioAgent Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21800v4): ten bioinformatics pipelines, including RNA-seq, variant calling, and metagenomics; corrupted-input, decoy-file, and prompt perturbations | Public [data downloader and reference pipelines](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-bench/tree/6d098b602b8a8fdc33a9d25e410a502be7ed9ce0) and [deterministic result checks](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/scoring.py) are released. Some checks accept limited overlap with reference outputs and need scientific review. | The [standard runner](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/taskset.py) also calls an LLM pipeline judge. The [supplied configuration](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/configs/eval/codex.toml) uses GPT-5.4-nano through OpenRouter. Adapt and validate the Together judge route; retain deterministic result checks and LLM-assessed progress as separate metrics. | Verifiers-based standalone runner. No adapter or integration issue found in `harbor-framework/harbor` or `marin-community/harbor` on 2026-09-15. Candidate for follow-up evaluation and a Harbor port; measure data, memory, and runtime needs first. |
| Follow-up | [sc-HeurekaBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01678): open-ended single-cell scientific reasoning | [Released benchmark and evaluator](https://github.com/mlbio-epfl/HeurekaBench/tree/c2a2b2fcdc5244220ff60f65483bc084c72a8cf1/scheurekabench) include 50 open-ended and 50 multiple-choice questions. | Open-answer scoring uses an LLM judge; the paper uses GPT-4o and reports judge/human agreement checks. Configure and validate a Together judge variant and data access. The multiple-choice scoring path has not been audited. | No adapter found. Follow-up scientific-reasoning comparison; report open-answer and multiple-choice metrics separately. |
| Follow-up | [Liu et al., single-cell agent benchmark](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-026-03998-z): 50 single-cell and multi-omics tasks | Public [evaluation pipeline](https://github.com/lyyang01/bioagent-benchmark/tree/1605e6e38bd69307e2f7b68a4367de21043c89b6/evaluation) and [Zenodo data/reference analyses](https://zenodo.org/records/17291196). Combines output consistency with code, execution, and knowledge-use metrics. | The standard pipeline requires an evaluation LLM; adapt and validate its Together integration. Distinguish reference-script similarity and aggregate process metrics from biological outcome correctness. Downloads and scorer execution remain untested. | No adapter found. Diagnostic workflow evaluation. This is a separate project from BioAgent Bench above. |
| Follow-up | [BAISBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.08341): single-cell annotation and data-grounded biological discovery | Public [evaluation notebooks](https://github.com/EperLuo/BaisBench/tree/cfab1beb09a7cba999c16f01475fdca37fee5cac) cover 15 annotated datasets and 193 multiple-choice questions from 41 studies. They provide an annotation metric and reference answers. | Multiple-choice answer-key scoring offers a route without an LLM judge. Data staging, extraction of agent answers, and annotation scoring need end-to-end validation. Keep reference answers outside the agent workspace. | No adapter found. Complementary single-cell evaluation; preserve the distinction between annotation and multiple-choice discovery scores. |
| Follow-up | [BioML-bench](https://github.com/science-machine/biomlbench/tree/673f3d8d3462fc6cdcbbd9695fba612b9332ca65): biomedical ML engineering across omics, proteins, imaging, and drug discovery | [Grading code](https://github.com/science-machine/biomlbench/blob/673f3d8d3462fc6cdcbbd9695fba612b9332ca65/biomlbench/grade.py) and task-specific numerical scorers are released; inspected examples use F1 and Pearson correlation. | No LLM judge in the inspected scorers. Check each source dataset's access, reference labels, and model-fitting compute requirements. The repository identifies the release as alpha. | MLE-bench-derived standalone runner; no adapter found. Complementary ML-engineering evaluation after selecting a bounded task. |
| Follow-up | [LABBench2](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2): broad research skills, including literature, sequences, and cloning | [HybridEvaluator](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2/blob/c028ecdcf144b55ffcd92b68be45081df5628c20/evals/evaluators.py) and sequence/cloning validators are released. Dataset includes answer and validator metadata; external reference files are resolved by the runner. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. `seqqa2` and `cloning` use executable grading. Other categories use an LLM judge, defaulting to Anthropic; even `exact_match_evaluator` calls an LLM. Validate provider/model changes for the Together route. | No LABBench2 adapter found. Existing Harbor `labbench` covers original LAB-Bench FigQA. Select complementary research-skill tasks by coverage; selection need not be limited to executable grading. |
| Follow-up | [CompBioBench](https://github.com/Genentech/compbiobench-runner): 100 tasks across omics, genetics, and ML | Official hosted scorer uses whitespace-stripped exact string match. Public runner and input dataset are released; no downloadable official scorer or answer key was found. The [leaderboard code](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Genentech/compbiobench-leaderboard-v1/blob/6a63e6d2cae531d9e9bf46b341606ed6b304ba3f/app.py) delegates grading to a separate evaluator that is not publicly accessible. | Hosted submission requires Hugging Face login, answers for all 100 questions, and currently allows two submissions per user per day. No OpenAI judge key is specified. | No adapter found. Full-suite hosted scoring is available through the documented submission path. A self-contained local verifier or small-subset scorer still needs author support. |
| Follow-up: long workflows | [BixBench3](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3): 20 research-scale analyses from raw data | [Artifact scorer](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3/blob/d0e0bbb41222335b1b8878f533a58466a3a782dc/src/bixbench3/grading/grader.py) is released, with reference artifact packages on GCS. `bixbench3 grade` scores existing artifacts deterministically. A separate process judge evaluates the analysis trajectory. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. Artifact scoring uses no LLM; the standard cloud runner uses OpenAI for process review and web-access decisions. Validate both functions when adapting to Together. Full artifact downloads were not tested. | Standalone runner; no adapter found. Later workflow evaluation, with data and runtime costs measured explicitly. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [BioMysteryBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/BioMysteryBench-full): analysis of anonymized biological datasets | Reference answers and criteria are supplied in `answer_rubric`. No official executable scorer was found in the release inventory or Anthropic GitHub search. Community scorers exist, but their equivalence to Anthropic's scoring is unverified. | Full 90-task release is gated and evaluation-only; five preview tasks and their rubrics are accessible. Rubrics require both a correct answer and compliance with the source-lookup policy, so checking answer text alone is insufficient. | No adapter found. Requires a specified grading procedure, such as documented expert review for a small diagnostic pilot; automated score comparability remains unresolved. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [BioXArena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15766): 76 biomedical ML tasks across nine domains | Public runner and input package; the pinned [release instructions](https://github.com/mbzuai-ai4bio/BioXArena/blob/29f88d4d573001405abf0694aee72d91c3f47e6c/README.md) state that test `answers.csv` is private. | Authors score submitted predictions against private answers. Published metrics are numerical; there is no verified self-contained local scoring route. Budget task-level model fitting separately from agent inference. | No adapter found. Requires arranging scoring and task compute before an evaluation commitment. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [EpiBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13602): epigenomics workflow steps across accessibility, chromatin, and methylation assays | Paper describes deterministic final-answer grading. The [public release](https://github.com/latchbio/epibench/tree/6bc01f15125f5a01ab78ce1fd2fc2c51c4ca04f3/evals) contains seven task JSONs; all omit grader configurations and target answers. | A deterministic method in the paper does not supply an executable local evaluation. Inputs are Latch data pointers; data access and task-specific scorer/target access remain unresolved. Full paper suite has 106 tasks. | No adapter found. Access-dependent candidate; obtain scoring assets before porting. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [SpatialBench-Long](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28065): study-scale spatial biological inference | Paper describes deterministic final-answer scoring and separate LLM-based trajectory rubrics. Four [public example packages](https://github.com/latchbio/spatialbench-long/tree/7de13d39ebbffee4db42675620fe0d97647e399e/evals) provide prompts/vocabularies; their task JSONs omit grader configurations and target answers. | Input access, scoring assets, and long-workflow resource budgets remain unresolved. Auxiliary LLM rubric scores must remain separate from deterministic benchmark pass/fail. | No adapter found. Later long-workflow comparison, conditional on access; public examples do not establish full-suite reproducibility. |

The literature search followed references in [BixBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.00096#S2), [BioAgent Bench](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21800v4#S9), and [GeneBench-Pro](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/21938268-21af-442f-af93-3b2249afb241/genebench-pro.pdf). Benchmark-specific sources and pinned release inventories are linked in the table.

Harbor availability above was checked in the adapter directories of [upstream `96a1354`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters) and [Marin `abdd671`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/abdd67137bcd6e5c44d682d0052fbd1190e63556/adapters). Recheck open issues and pull requests before starting a port. Public task counts describe the pinned release inventories; they must not be substituted for the task counts behind published leaderboard scores.

Choose the first suite by scientific relevance, integration effort, grading availability, and measured cost. Record whether an LLM is needed for correctness grading, process review, or other runner functions.

Prioritize BixBench's existing Harbor CLI route for the first primary-suite readiness check: configure the Together judge, validate scoring on known answers, and verify that one real analysis can execute. Continue the prepared Terminal-Bench-Science smoke test to validate Snowball serving and terminal execution. ScienceAgentBench is the next integrated bioinformatics candidate; choose tasks by relevance and resource needs, with visual judging validated where used. Follow-up ports and standalone suites remain in the table. Expand to a measured pilot only after readiness checks, excluding development smoke-test tasks. The inspected `genomic-model-ranking` task specifies 2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM, no GPU, and an eight-hour agent limit; the diagnostic Snowball configuration caps the agent at 15 minutes and must be reported as a different budget.

Scorer validation: at GeneBench-Pro release `eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2`, the reference grader accepted the published reference answer for all 10 cases and rejected deliberately wrong and empty answer objects for all 10. These 30 checks ran locally without an API or analysis data. They validate the grading interface, not the scientific analyses. The documented command is `python3 reference_grader.py <eval_config.json> <eval_answer.json>`. A future adapter must expose only the task, answer schema, and analysis inputs to the agent; keep the full config, references, tolerances, reports, and grader outside its workspace.

## Status

No Snowball computational biology baseline has completed. The Terminal-Bench-Science `genomic-model-ranking` oracle completed through Harbor/Daytona on September 14 with reward 1 (Iris job `/gonzalo/bio-9160-oracle-20260914-210913`; artifacts: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/bio-9160-oracle-20260914-210913/results`). Two subsequent Snowball serving attempts ended after endpoint-readiness timeouts without obtaining GPU capacity. The expanded benchmark survey provides alternatives for evaluation coverage; no agent runs, hosted submissions, or data-access requests were made for the new candidates. The proposed October 6, 2026 target for the post-trained 67B Snowball release motivates obtaining the baseline beforehand, subject to serving availability.

First milestone:

- [ ] Select a primary benchmark and record the checkpoint, evaluation owner, serving contact, budget, and target date.
- [ ] Confirm a working endpoint or serving allocation, sandbox access, and Together judge configuration. Record the Together billing owner and pilot judge budget before paid calls. Budget serving time, sandbox task-hours, grading, setup, and retries separately.
- [ ] Pin model/tokenizer, Marin/Harbor, dataset, and container revisions. Record prompts, tools/network policy, sampling, context management, context/step/time limits, judge settings, and retry policy.
- [ ] Validate one or two development tasks: reference answers pass, deliberately wrong answers fail, missing submissions are accounted for, and a real analysis can execute. Keep reference answers, solutions, and verifier material inaccessible to the solving agent. The BixBench oracle writes an answer directly, so it checks grading without reproducing the analysis.
- [ ] Run one prespecified task once and measure serving time, sandbox time, and grading cost. Expand to 5–10 prespecified tasks only after checking the measured cost against the pilot budget; retain the first task in that pilot. Exclude the development smoke-test tasks from the measured pilot. For BixBench, select questions from distinct data capsules (separate source notebooks and their associated data) and record their IDs before examining their Snowball results.
- [ ] Publish configs, trajectories, produced artifacts, success counts, coverage, runtime/cost, and a short failure analysis. Report successes over all scheduled attempts and over attempts with a determined model outcome. Coverage is the fraction of scheduled attempts with a determined model outcome. Count agent-caused missing submissions and timeouts as failures unless a retained verifier result establishes success. Exclude unresolved infrastructure and grader errors only from the second denominator; report their counts and coverage separately.
- [ ] Decide whether to expand the primary suite, repair the harness, or validate a second benchmark. Record the evidence and follow-up owner.

For subsequent checkpoint comparisons, hold the task set, harness, and execution budget fixed. Keep inspected development tasks separate from an untouched final evaluation set. Preserve each baseline and record protocol changes. Evaluation-only materials and inspected evaluation trajectories must stay out of training.

Treat all ten public GeneBench-Pro cases as development and reproduction material for this effort. Any final set whose results have not guided model or protocol changes must be selected separately before follow-on training; the initial pilot does not supply that final set.

Count each fresh agent rollout, including retries, as a separate attempt and report first-attempt success separately. Regrading an existing submission does not create a new agent attempt.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
An interrupted Hugging Face checkpoint mirror leaves uploaded shards in regional object storage, but retrying downloads and uploads them again. The GLM-5.2 attempt left approximately 295 GB under its pinned cache prefix; the retry overwrote existing shards instead of resuming. At approximately 106 MB/s, repeating the 474 GB snapshot exceeds evaluation's 40-minute startup budget.

Reproduce:
1. Start `cache_hf_model` for a pinned multi-shard checkpoint in an empty prefix.
2. Terminate the worker after several shards upload, before `.cache_metadata.json` is written.
3. Retry against the same prefix and revision. Previously uploaded shard modification times change, and Hugging Face downloads repeat.

Expected: validate existing shards against the pinned source metadata and skip matching objects; download missing or mismatched objects. Use size and a reliable content identity/checksum, not an assumption that every object-store ETag is an MD5. Preserve the distributed lock and write the existing completion marker only after every required file is validated. Cover interruption and resume, mismatched objects, and complete-cache hits in tests.

`lib/levanter/src/levanter/model_cache.py:228` (`_stream_hf_snapshot`) unconditionally downloads and uploads each file. `cache_to_prefix` only recognizes the final completion marker. No implementation is included in this report.

[Incident evidence and affected runs](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/468). Found during #8215 validation.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Research: _stream_hf_snapshot downloads every repository file whenever the snapshot completion marker is absent; uploaded shards are not checked. Both automatic serving preparation and the standalone CPU job use this path.

Proposed Fix: fetch pinned Hugging Face file metadata, verify existing objects by size and content hash (LFS SHA-256 or Git blob SHA-1), and skip verified files. Retain the distributed lock and final marker. This reads existing regional objects during recovery but avoids re-downloading them over the internet; no object-store ETag assumptions. Add interruption/resume and corrupt-object regression coverage.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
When an evaluation serves a model from Hugging Face, the model weights are downloaded by the GPU serving job itself, as the first thing it does before starting vLLM. The evaluation orchestrator waits at most 2400 seconds (`ENDPOINT_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` in `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/serving_config.py`) for the endpoint to come up, and that budget has to cover both the download and vLLM startup. For large checkpoints the download alone takes longer than the budget, so the orchestrator times out and terminates the serving job. Two problems follow: the GPUs sit idle for the whole download, and the timeout kills the download partway through.

Observed with GLM-5.2 (`cyankiwi/GLM-5.2-AWQ-INT4`, 474 GB in 83 weight shards). Job `/karan/eval-20260916-190154-glm-5.2-awq-int4-pp2-1m-3ac6` started mirroring at 19:04 UTC on 2026-09-16 at roughly 106 MB/s and timed out at 19:42 UTC with about 295 GB uploaded. Sixteen H100s were reserved for the full 38 minutes and did no inference. A retry on 2026-09-17 hit the same deadline, so the weights were finally mirrored by a hand-submitted CPU-only job, which took about 70 minutes. Incident record: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/468.

How the jobs fit together today. The eval CLI submits one CPU orchestrator job (`run_evaluation_batch` in `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py`). The orchestrator submits a GPU child job for inference (`_start_direct_inference` in `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`). Inside that GPU job, `resolve_model_path` mirrors the Hugging Face repo into the region bucket under a lock and writes a completion marker, and only then does vLLM start. Iris has no job dependency primitive, so ordering between jobs is done by the orchestrator waiting on children.

Proposal: prepare the weights in a separate CPU job before the GPU job is submitted.

- Before submitting the inference job, the orchestrator checks whether the pinned checkpoint already has a completion marker in the region cache.
- On a miss, it submits a small CPU child job (for example `prepare-<run_id>`) that calls the existing mirror function, and waits for it with its own timeout sized for the download rather than for vLLM startup. The job needs enough disk for one shard at a time (about 30 GB for GLM-5.2) and the same region constraint as the GPU job, so the mirror stays in-region.
- The GPU job is submitted only after the prepare job succeeds. Its own `resolve_model_path` call then finds the marker and returns immediately, so nothing in the serving path changes.
- The 2400-second readiness deadline then covers only vLLM startup, which is what it was sized for.

Expected: launching an evaluation against a large uncached checkpoint reserves GPUs only once the weights are in the region cache, and a slow download fails the cheap prepare job instead of the GPU job.

Related: #9230 covers reusing shards that were already uploaded before a mirror was interrupted. That makes an interrupted prepare job resumable, and is independent of this change. #8215 is the pipeline-parallel serving work that first hit this on GLM-5.2. Setting `HF_TOKEN` on the prepare job may raise the download rate, since the current mirror runs unauthenticated and Hugging Face rate-limits anonymous requests.

Done when: an evaluation launch against an uncached large checkpoint runs a CPU prepare job first, the GPU inference job starts with a cache hit, and a test with a fake Iris client covers the miss, hit, and prepare-failure paths.

spillover_issues.author: lukedhlee
spillover_issues.body:
I evaluated the Snowball R2E-Gym RL checkpoints under [Eval Policy v0.1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193) (harbor `7b18505a`, the recovery job files from `8aa9a354`, one trial per task, 16 concurrent, 32,768 / 8,192 tokens, terminus-2 defaults, Daytona). Two things came out that I think matter beyond Snowball. Full write-up with the training-side story: https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/01897efa3ae7c474732c61d35150a43a (Part III).

**Checkpoints.** Base = [laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888). RL = GRPO on R2E-Gym repository-fix tasks with terminus-2 (terminal only), [old stack update 36](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-oldstack-step36) and [new stack update 24](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step24), the pick. Two later checkpoints are in the figure too: [update 48](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step48) of the same run, and update 24 continued for 24 more updates on a refreshed pool of 1,247 tasks. Training ran terminus-2 with summarization **off** at 49,152 input / 16,384 output tokens.

### 1. The RL gain is in-distribution: SWE-bench Verified moves, Terminal-Bench 2 does not

![Under Marin's eval policy, the RL gain shows on SWE-bench and not on Terminal-Bench 2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/3998f0fb24fe70f1d6aa7d55fa575b2255bc51e9/fig5_policy_id_vs_ood.png)

Whiskers are 95% intervals, about ±8 points with one trial per task. Paired on SWE-bench the new checkpoint solves 15 tasks the base does not and loses 4 (12 to 8 against the old stack). On TB2 the base and the two RL picks are within noise and update 24 is lowest in every setting I tried. Training longer does not move SWE-bench: update 48 scores 25 against update 24's 23 and wins 13 tasks while losing 11, the same churn two identical runs of update 24 show (23 and 24, disagreeing on 22 tasks). The refreshed pool did not buy transfer: 17 on SWE-bench, losing 16 tasks to update 24 and winning 10, and 5 of 89 on TB2. The one hint of anything is update 48 on TB2, 9 of 87 against 4, winning 6 and losing 1, still inside a one-trial interval. TB2 denominators are scored tasks; 0 to 4 trials per run were lost to infrastructure (mostly the agent running `pkill -f` inside the sandbox, which kills harbor's own tmux command), inside the 10 % allowance, and counting them as failures does not change the order.

R2E-Gym and SWE-bench are the same kind of work, a Python repo with failing tests to fix, and that is where the 11 points show up. The RL checkpoint declares done fast (median 4 minutes of agent time per SWE-bench task vs 21 for the base), which is what finishing inside the window looks like on repo fixes and what giving up early looks like on TB2's long build-and-verify tasks.

### 2. Summarization helps the RL checkpoint, even though it was never trained with it

SWE-bench random-100 at the policy setting, at 32k with summarization off, and at the training setting (49k/16k, off), for base and the new checkpoint:

![How each SWE-bench trial ended, by terminus-2 setting](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/cac4e15e3f7d8f684aa35b7bddb24ec58bdd5042/fig6_summarization_context.png)

All 600 trials scored, no infrastructure losses. A trial that runs out of context stops and is graded as it stands. Caveat: the base's two summarization-off rows were served at temperature 0.7 with a repetition penalty of 1.1 by mistake; every other row is temperature 1.0 with no penalty. It cannot change the picture for a model that overflows on 97 of 100 tasks, but those two rows are not sampler-paired with the rest. Agent requests in all runs set `skip_special_tokens: false` so the think markers stay in the transcript; Marin's agentic launcher does not set this flag today. A paired probe says it does not matter for the score: the RL checkpoint at the policy setting scores 23 and 24 of 100 with the flag (two runs) and 23 without it, and the two flag-on runs disagree on as many tasks (22) as flag-on vs flag-off (23), so per-task differences are sampling noise at temperature 1.0.

- The base cannot work without summarization: 94 to 97 of 100 trials overflow at either budget. RL cut that to 42 at the training budget.
- The RL checkpoint's best number is with summarization on, which training never used, and its lead over base is the same size in every setting (+11, +5, +11). RL improved the task skill rather than fitting one context regime.
- Summarization at 32k beats a 49k window without it, for both models. 23 vs 19 is inside the one-trial noise; a 3-trial rerun (~15 GH200 node-hours) would settle it.

**Takeaways for the policy.** Keeping terminus-2's summarization on in v0.1 is the right call for this model family, and it is not a mismatch with how the checkpoint was trained. SWE-bench random-100 is the ID leg that detects R2E-Gym RL; TB2 does not, at this checkpoint.

**Reproduction.** Stack, task revisions (DCAgent2/terminal_bench_2, DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders `0c553bd6`) and the variant configs are in the gist's "Policy evaluation" section. Job directories and traces are on JSC Jupiter; happy to attach any trial.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis (not a PR):** This is a research/prototyping + benchmarking task (reproducible FP8 run path, MFU/timing/memory measurement on TPU, ≥40% speedup target). Per the agent workflow it's out of scope for an auto-PR — posting root-cause/code map and a proposed approach for a human (matt) to drive.

# Research

FP8 quant exists (`Fp8DotGeneralOp`, `quantize_linear_layers`) and is wired into the dense `Linear` layer via its `dot_general` field, but the MoE expert path runs through `ragged_dot` (grouped matmul / megablox on TPU) which has **no** quantization hook — `MoELinear` explicitly leaves it as a TODO. So an FP8 expert GMM path does not exist today and must be built where `ragged_dot` is called.

**Relevant code**
- [`linear.py#L194-L200`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/linear.py#L194-L200) — `MoELinear` with `# TODO: support quantization for ragged_dot?` (no `dot_general` field)
- [`linear.py#L233-L310`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/linear.py#L233-L310) — `MoELinear.__call__` / `_gmm`, the expert matmul call sites
- [`ragged_dot.py#L67-L392`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py#L67-L392) — `ragged_dot()` + megablox/Triton/XLA backends (the GMM to quantize)
- [`fp8.py#L122-L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/_src/fp8.py#L122-L150) — `dot_general_with_precision`, the FP8 QDQ matmul primitive to reuse
- [`quantization.py#L154-L256`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/quantization.py#L154-L256) — `Fp8DotGeneralOp`, `QuantizationConfig`, `quantize_linear_layers`

# Proposed Approach

Minimal prototype → benchmark, in three steps:

1. **Add an FP8 GMM path.** Introduce a quantized variant alongside `ragged_dot` plumbed to per-group e4m3fn QDQ of activations + expert weights, reusing the QDQ machinery in `fp8.py`. On TPU the megablox `gmm` accepts low-precision operands directly; start there and keep the XLA path as a numeric reference. Gate it behind a config flag on `MoEExpertMlp` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`) / `MoELinear` rather than the dense-`Linear` `Fp8DotGeneralOp` (which doesn't cover ragged_dot).
2. **Reproducible run path.** Wire the flag through the MoE config so a single config toggles bf16↔fp8 for a known model (Mixtral / Qwen3-MoE / grug MoE). Record the exact branch + launch command in this issue.
3. **Measure** on one TPU config: forward+backward timing and MFU bf16 vs fp8 (target ≥40%), peak HBM, and a numerical/stability check (cosine sim / max-abs-err of expert outputs and grads, plus a short loss-curve sanity run) — fp8 e4m3 for fwd, consider e5m2 for grads.

Open questions for matt before implementation: (a) which model/scale is the baseline; (b) TPU generation (v5e/v6e — affects whether megablox fp8 is supported in the pinned JAX); (c) scope to forward-only fp8 first, or fwd+bwd. Happy to implement step 1 as a scoped PR once the target model/hardware is fixed.

# Proposed Approach (for @rav to run)

**128-GPU mesh.** `SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS=16` (16×8=128). With default `SCALE_EXPERT_AXIS=8`, `SCALE_REPLICA_AXIS=1`: `data_axis=128/8=16`, `batch_shards=1*16*8=128` → `SCALE_BATCH` must be a multiple of **128**.

**Max-BS sweep** (find OOM boundary; mem ∝ batch×seq, replicated FSDP intermediate per L64-67):
```
RUN_ID=bs-sweep SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS=16 SCALE_BATCH={128,256,384,512} \
  SCALE_STEPS=20 SCALE_CHECKPOINTS=local SCALE_TRACKER=wandb \
  SCALE_PROFILER_STEPS=5 uv run experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py
```

**XLA flags** — set via the launcher shell, forwarded by `dispatch.py`. Candidates for fwd+bwd throughput: `--xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=true`, `--xla_gpu_enable_pipelined_all_gather/reduce_scatter/all_reduce=true`, `--xla_gpu_all_reduce_combine_threshold_bytes` / `all_gather_combine_threshold_bytes` tuning. Parent tracker: #6693

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + parent tracker #6693 (accepts "SM90 row visible **or code-path proof**")
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (FA4 PRs/issues)
- [x] Trace FA4 arch dispatch on H100/SM90
- [x] Confirm production Grug d2560 shape (head_dim, GQA)
- [x] Post code-path proof + what's needed to fully close

This is verification work, not a code change — no PR. Fully closing the DoD needs the May215/`FA4PROFILE` artifact + an H100 profiling run (neither reachable from this environment), so this comment supplies the **code-path proof** half of the parent's acceptance bar.

# Research

On H100 (compute capability 9.0 → `arch=90`), the production Grug MoE attention shape routes the FA4/CuTe **backward** through the native upstream SM90 launcher added in #6613. The forward is the arch-agnostic Grug segmented CuTe kernel (no native-SM90 variant); only the backward has the SM80/SM120-compat vs native-SM90 split, and the backward is what May208 flagged as the top hotspot (#6613).

The native SM90 backward is gated on three conditions, all satisfied by the production d2560 shape:

1. `kernel_config.sm90_backward is not None` — set only for `arch_family == 9` (H100).
2. `qhead_per_kvhead > 1` — GQA. Production uses 4:1.
3. `q.shape[-1] == 128` — head_dim 128. Production `hidden_head_ratio=128` ⇒ `head_dim == 128`.

Otherwise the path falls back to `segmented_flash_attention_backward_launcher(..., compute_arch=90)` — compiled for SM90 but the slower segmented fork, i.e. the pre-#6613 behavior. So "FA4 SM90 active" hinges precisely on the shape being D128 GQA; MHA or non-128 head_dim silently takes the compat launcher even on SM90.

**Relevant code**
- [`_fa4_cute.py#L117-L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py#L117-L128) — `_gpu_compute_arch()`, H100 → `arch=90`
- [`_fa4_cute_config.py#L68-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_config.py#L68-L80) — `arch_family==9` sets `backward_arch=90` + `sm90_backward`
- [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158-L182`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158-L182) — native SM90 gate (`sm90_backward is not None and GQA and D128`)
- [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L184-L196`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L184-L196) — compat fallback `compute_arch=backward_arch`
- [`heuristic.py#L113-L114`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/heuristic.py#L113-L114) — `hidden_head_ratio=128` ⇒ head_dim 128, GQA 4:1

# Proposed approach (for the owner, @rav)

Code-path proof above is sufficient for the parent's "code-path proof" branch. To also satisfy the DoD's *per-step attribution report with FA4 timing/share*:

1. **Confirm in the existing profile.** Point the xprof analysis (`.agents/skills/profile-training/SKILL.md`) at the May215 / `…-FA4PROFILE-…` XPlane. The native SM90 backward shows as upstream `FlashAttentionBackwardSm90` kernels (preprocess + mainloop + postprocess, [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L274-L290`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L274-L290)); the compat path shows the segmented backward launcher instead. Presence of the former = SM90 active.
2. **Or a fresh readable proof.** A short H100 run on the d2560 shape with `enable_hlo_proto=true` (SKILL.md "profile options") yields named-scope attribution; assert the backward kernel name is the SM90 variant and report its per-step share.
3. **If inactive:** the only realistic miss is the shape not meeting the D128-GQA gate at [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158) — verify `qhead_per_kvhead`/`head_dim` on the launched config rather than assuming the heuristic default.
